display: Nursing student in Ho Chi Minh City, trained in wound dressing, volunteering at a pagoda free clinic on weekends.

signals.text: My night rotation ends at 10pm and the last bus leaves at 9:30. I need a safe, affordable way home a few nights a week.
Getting home after night shifts takes a big share of my monthly budget, and I'm looking for ways to cut that cost.
My roommate is moving out next month, and I need a quiet, reliable person to share rent with, or a cheaper room near District 5.
I'm preparing for an English-for-nursing exam. My reading is fine, but my pronunciation is weak and I want someone to practise speaking with.
I have a pharmacology midterm on 15 October and I'm looking for a study partner.
A professor suggested I consider a graduate program, but I don't know how anyone pays for it. I'd like to hear from people who found funding.
I want to work in pediatric or emergency care and am looking for mentors who have done that work.
Night shifts on the surgical ward are tiring, and some cases stay with me afterwards. I'd like to talk with someone who works in healthcare.
I can't take paid work during my rotation. I'd like small ways to ease living costs that don't need a regular job.
My family's farm back home was hit by a flood, and I want to help but can't do much from here.
The pagoda clinic day could use more hands and basic supplies for checking blood pressure for elderly people.
My family owes money to a local cooperative after last year's disease outbreak, and I'd like to learn how other families got through it.

offers.text: I'm a third-year nursing student trained in wound dressing and doing clinical rotations, with a signed log of procedures.
I hold a basic life support (BLS) certificate, valid until next March.
I can take blood pressure and run a small health-check station at community or charity events on weekends.
I can teach a short, practical first-aid or wound-care session to a small group, in Vietnamese.
I'm fluent in Vietnamese and have working English. I can explain basic health information in plain language to elderly people and to families from the countryside.
I know every bus route and walking route around District 5, and I can give newcomers directions or a route plan.
I keep nursing vocabulary notes from drama subtitles and flashcards, and I'm happy to swap them with other nursing or English learners.
I scored 8.5 in pharmacology and can study together with a classmate who needs a partner.
I'm free on weekends outside rotation shifts and can volunteer at health or charity events.
I grew up in a Mekong Delta village, so I understand rural families' health habits and the barriers they face in getting care.

catchers.hypo: Hi, I coordinate volunteers for a free community health day in Ho Chi Minh City. We need someone who can check blood pressure and help elderly people feel comfortable. Do you know anyone?
catchers.can: I can help in person on weekends outside my rotation, bring my own BP cuff, and introduce the organizers to the pagoda clinic team I already volunteer with.
catchers.confirm: Is the event on a weekend, in or near Ho Chi Minh City, and does it need only basic checks rather than any treatment?

catchers.hypo: I run an English speaking club for health students. We practise medical vocabulary out loud and we need one more regular member.
catchers.can: I'd join as a regular speaking partner and bring nursing vocabulary lists to share.
catchers.confirm: Does the club meet on a day or evening when a nursing student on night rotations could attend, and is it free?

catchers.hypo: I'm a nurse in Ho Chi Minh City. Pediatric and emergency nursing both took me years, and I can mentor a student who is still deciding between them.
catchers.can: I'd take the mentoring seriously. I'd also ask my clinical supervisor, a senior nurse, whether she is open to a conversation with you, if that would help.
catchers.confirm: Do you currently work in pediatric or emergency nursing, and can you talk with a student for about half an hour?

catchers.hypo: I'm a nursing student with a quiet lifestyle, and I'm looking for a room share near District 5 starting next month.
catchers.can: I can tell you about the room, and my current roommate Mai, who is moving out, could introduce you and her classmate who was already proposed as a replacement.
catchers.confirm: Are you a student or health worker who needs a quiet place, and can you move in next month and split the rent evenly?

catchers.hypo: I organize a late-evening shuttle or carpool for hospital and clinic staff near District 5. We have an open seat after 10pm.
catchers.can: I'd use it on my night-shift days, and I could tell other student nurses about it.
catchers.confirm: Does the ride leave the district hospital area around 10pm and drop off in or near District 5?

catchers.hypo: I work in aquaculture extension in the Mekong Delta. Flooded shrimp ponds and cooperative debt are common problems, and I'd like to share options with a family in Ben Tre.
catchers.can: I could pass your contact to my mother in Ben Tre, who raises shrimp, so she can decide whether to talk with you.
catchers.confirm: Are you an extension officer, cooperative advisor or similar professional who can give practical help to small shrimp farmers, not a lender or seller of products?

catchers.hypo: I run a scholarship or mentoring program for nursing graduates who want a master's degree, and I'd like to meet strong students from rural backgrounds.
catchers.can: I could share my pharmacology results and transcript, and talk about what I'd want to study.
catchers.confirm: Does the program cover tuition or living costs for graduate nursing study, and does it accept students from outside the big cities?

catchers.hypo: I'm a hospital recruiter looking for nursing students with English skills and clinical experience for a unit that treats international patients.
catchers.can: I'd talk about my skills and the English exam score I'm working toward, and give you my rotation supervisor's name as a reference once I'm ready.
catchers.confirm: Is the role for a student or new graduate, and does it accept an English exam score that is still in progress?

forbids.text: I can't take paid jobs during my clinical rotation.
I don't have a motorbike or a driver's licence, so I can't take on tasks that need me to drive.
I can't give medical diagnoses or treatment advice. I'm a student and can only offer basic care within my training.
Nothing that puts my scholarship at risk, since I must keep my GPA above 3.0.
I'm not available on rotation night shifts, roughly 3pm to 10pm, a few days a week.
I won't share my allowance amount or my bank details with anyone.
I don't walk home alone late at night on the quiet roads near the canal.

policy.t1: When there is a real lead, I can share my rotation schedule, the late-night transport problem, and how much the commute weighs on my monthly budget, without exact figures.
policy.t2: Once the person's identity is clear and trust is high, I can tell them about my family's debt and the flooded shrimp pond, and consider introducing them to my mother.
policy.never: My full allowance, my bank details, and my family's exact finances.
